KiloQuest has no ads, no tracking and no analytics, and no account.

On this device only: points, stickers, settings, figures, the travel diary and photos. Nothing of this is uploaded. Backups of the app data are switched off. You can delete single photo entries, the whole diary, or export everything as a ZIP file in Settings.

Services that receive requests (your IP address and the places needed for the request, no name, no account):
• Your own routing server (routes, speed limits): your server may log requests; you are its operator.
• Photon / komoot (place search, country of a position), Overpass API (rest stops, viewpoints), OpenFreeMap (map tiles), Wikipedia (stories), Open-Meteo (weather), iNaturalist (animal quests), Autobahn API (German traffic).

Paired devices exchange game state, route, position of the car, speed and distance only via Bluetooth, and only with devices you allowed.

Camera and microphone: the camera is used only when the co-driver taps "Take photo"; the microphone only for voice answers and, if you switch it on, for commands with the name "Kilo". Speech is recognised on the device and is not stored, unless you explicitly allow the normal speech service of the phone in the settings (then the provider of that service may receive the recording). Photos are re-encoded without location data.

Details: docs/legal/datenschutz.md in the project.

You have heard the whole series. What an adventure!

Episode one: The lost compass. Kilo packs the family car for the journey to %1$s. At the bottom of the bag Kilo finds an old star compass that glows softly. Its needle does not point north. It points to %1$s! Then the compass gives a tiny tick, and a voice whispers: Follow me. To be continued!

Episode two: The night owl. The compass leads Kilo along a long, dark road. In a tree sits a big owl with golden eyes. I know where the compass wants to go, says the owl, but first you must find three lights. Kilo looks out of the window and counts the lights of the road. One, two, and then... what is that glowing in the sky? To be continued!

Episode three: The bridge troll. At a huge bridge a grumpy troll blocks the way. Only those who answer my riddle may cross, he grumbles. What goes up and down but never moves? Kilo thinks and thinks. A staircase! The troll laughs so hard that he almost falls into the water. Please take my gift, he says, and gives Kilo a tiny silver key. But what does the key open? To be continued!

Episode four: The ferry whale. The way leads across the sea. On the ferry, the silver key suddenly glows. A huge whale rises beside the ship and sings a deep, slow song. The key fits into the whale\'s song, and the compass shows a new light: the lights of the north are waiting! But the sky is getting dark. To be continued!

Episode five: The northern lights fox. At night green and purple ribbons dance across the sky. A snow-white fox sits on a hill. The star compass sleeps here, says the fox, but it needs a friend to wake it up. Everyone in the car must say one kind word. Kilo starts, and the compass begins to shine brighter than ever. To be continued!

Episode six: Arrival in %1$s. At last the family arrives in %1$s. The star compass rises into the air, spins around, and drops tiny stars on the snow. It was never lost, whispers Kilo. It wanted to bring a family together on a big adventure. And that is exactly what happened. The end. Until the next journey!

Warning: audio may leave the phone

Without an offline speech pack, Android uses the normal speech recognition service of this phone (usually from Google or the phone maker). The recording of what is said in the car can then be sent to that provider\'s servers and may be processed under its privacy terms. This includes voice commands, spoken quiz answers and audio games, so the voices of children can be recorded.\n\nKiloQuest itself stores and sends nothing. Allow this only if you understand and accept it, and only as long as you really need it. Better: download the offline speech pack in the voice input settings. You can switch this off at any time.
